card.name: Biyelgee
card.tagline: Mongolia's body dance — UNESCO-listed Urgent Safeguarding tradition where the dancer's body becomes the steppe itself.
card.profile: Biyelgee (Mongolian Cyrillic: Биелгээ) or Bii (Mongolian Cyrillic: Бий), is a traditional dance from Mongolia. Most of the country's regions have their own forms. The Western Mongols (Oirats) are particularly famous for their Biyelgee dance.
card.insight: UNESCO inscribed Biyelgee on the List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding in 2009 — recognising that the tradition was at risk as Mongolia urbanised away from its nomadic roots. The dance's defining feature is its constraint: performed inside a ger with no floor space, every movement is from the waist up, with the body retelling a pastoral life — milking the goats, drawing the bow, riding the horse — through pure upper-body gesture.
